summary: API LB buffering + header growth causing in-flight streaming starvation and intermittent 504/502s
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent stream stalls and downstream 504/502 responses during long-running streaming completions. Impact: Several of ByteCart's production endpoints experienced short periods where streaming sessions received no bytes for 10-40s and then aborted with 502 or 504; user-facing failures and cancellations increased ~4x during windows. Environment: Dedicated route in prod (us-east-1) serving redwood-chat-2b pinned model. Observed during peak morning traffic windows. Hypothesis: API gateway / LB is buffering/coalescing small chunks while per-connection header metadata (tracing/tenant headers) grows over time, hitting internal buffering thresholds or idle-send timers which then trigger resets.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ByteCart's production route in us-east-1 with long streaming completion (>60s) and client that sends frequent small chunked requests and rotates an X-Trace header per chunk. 2) Observe TTFB and streaming health via curl/wget with --no-buffer or via the SDK. 3) During load, watch for idle periods where no bytes are forwarded for 10-40s and then connection resets with 502/504. 4) Reproduction was confirmed on a canary traffic profile that mimicked ByteCart's chunking pattern.

2026-03-10 09:25 - Mateo Ruiz (SRE): Initial triage indicates apigw idle-send timer fired when header growth exceeded 8KB buffer thresh. Reproduced locally with rotated tracing header pattern. Opening SRE investigation.

investigation_notes: Reproduced: Yes — reproduced in our canary environment when client rotated a 2KB tracing header every 1-2s and sent frequent 256B body chunks. When aggregated header metadata exceeded the apigw internal coalescing threshold, apigw deferred sends and triggered idle-send timers.

Observed correlation with serving-runtime KV cache warmup. During warmup latencies spike and request pacing increases; that combination increases buffering pressure in apigw, causing longer coalescing windows.
Heap/descriptor usage on apigw nodes peaked during the window but did not OOM. No 5xx at serving-runtime level; errors were introduced by proxy resets at the load balancer layer.

Config review: ALB idle timeout defaulted to 60s for customer route. Apigw had proxy_buffering enabled for performance; this interacts poorly with high-frequency small-chunk uploads and rotating headers.
Mitigation tested: disabling proxy_buffering eliminates silent periods in local repro. Increasing ALB idle timeout prevents premature connection reset but does not eliminate buffering-induced pauses.

Next steps: 1) implement route-level apigw config toggle for proxy_buffering per-customer, 2) add telemetry to measure header-growth and buffered bytes per-connection, 3) add note to runbook about interaction with KV-cache warmup and small-chunk workloads.
resolution: Mitigation applied: For ByteCart's dedicated route we disabled apigw proxy_buffering and increased ALB idle timeout to 90s (infra PR-4281). Short-term outcome: streaming failures dropped by ~90% in the monitored window; remaining stalls correlated with KV-cache warmup which we are investigating. Long-term plan: expose proxy_buffering toggle per-route, add per-connection buffered_bytes metric to Console, and update runbook. Follow-up owner: Mateo Ruiz (SRE) to validate changes over 72h and schedule a postmortem if residual customer impact persists. Customer will confirm closure after 72h monitoring.
